sections.html:
Elmore County lies in east central Alabama, just north of Montgomery, and is part of the Montgomery metro area. Wetumpka is the seat and Millbrook is the largest city. The land sits on the fall line, so it runs from rolling hills to open farm fields, with river frontage in Wetumpka and Tallassee. A house description should say what kind of lot comes with it.

Elmore is one of Alabama's fastest-growing counties. Population went from 49,210 in 1990 to 65,874 in 2000, 79,303 in 2010 and 87,977 in 2020, with a 2025 estimate of 91,577. The 2020 census found 32,567 households in 36,818 housing units, and 11.5 percent of the units were vacant. Owners occupy 76.0 percent of occupied homes, the homeowner vacancy rate is 1.5 percent and the rental vacancy rate is 6.5 percent. About 71 percent of residents live in rural areas.

Sellers range from long-time river-town owners to commuters in newer subdivisions. The Elmore County Public School System serves most of the county, and part of it falls in the Tallassee City School District. A buyer will ask which system covers an address, so confirm it before you list or accept an offer.

The four cities are Prattville (partly in Autauga County), Millbrook (partly in Autauga County), Tallassee (partly in Tallapoosa County) and Wetumpka. The four towns are Coosada, Deatsville, Eclectic and Elmore, and Blue Ridge, Emerald Mountain, Holtville and Redland are census-designated places.

The county line cuts through several of these places, and that decides where a deed is recorded and who bills the tax. A parcel in the Autauga part of Prattville or Millbrook belongs to a different county than one in Elmore's part. Look at your tax bill before you contact any office.

Elmore voters approved a single Revenue Commissioner on March 6, 1990, under Act No. 90-254, and that office combined the jobs of tax assessor and tax collector. It covers about 44,000 parcels across roughly 630 square miles and also values business personal property and personal aircraft.

The office is at 100 E. Commerce Street, Suite 102, in Wetumpka, open Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The phone number is 334-567-1184. A Citizen Access Portal and a parcel viewer are linked from the county's website, and both are handy for looking up your own record before you sell.

October 1 is the due date and December 31 the delinquency date. Unpaid accounts then follow the statewide sequence toward a probate court sale.

DateStep
October 1Tax due
January 1Delinquent
FebruaryTurned over to the Probate Court
MarchProbate Court meets
AprilAdvertised for sale
MayTax sale

Interest and penalties are added to past-due balances, so call the Revenue Commissioner for the exact charge on your account.

Voters in the late 1990s also passed a mandatory fire fee for volunteer fire services. Every citizen pays the same amount, whatever the value of the property or the person's income, so it does not change with your assessment. Ask the county how the fee is billed.

The state's recording privilege tax is fifty cents per $500 of value under Alabama Code 40-22-1. The probate recording fee is separate. Of the tax collected, two-thirds goes to the state treasury and one-third to the county treasury.

The sale price must be certified on the Department of Revenue form. A deed without proof of price can be taxed on the latest assessment and draw a penalty of $100 or 25 percent of the tax, whichever is greater. After a sale, the new owner records the deed with the probate office and then takes it to the Revenue Commissioner to have the property assessed.

Typical situations include inherited houses in Wetumpka or Tallassee with no one living in them, rentals where a tenant moved out in a fast-growing market, river houses with deferred repairs, and owners behind on tax as the May sale approaches.

A cash purchase can clear the tax and take the house as is, which avoids the cost of preparing it for a retail listing.

  1. Check your tax bill to confirm which county holds the parcel.
  2. Call the Revenue Commissioner for the balance on each tax year.
  3. Gather the deed and, for an inherited house, the probate papers.
  4. Ask the title company to confirm every payoff before closing.

For a house near the river, find any flood paperwork and repair receipts first. For a house in a new subdivision, find the builder's warranty papers if they still apply. These small items answer a buyer's first questions.

A house nobody lives in is the easiest to lose track of. Bills pile up at the old address, grass grows and neighbors start to wonder. If you inherited a house in Wetumpka or Tallassee, begin with the basics: who is on the deed, which years of tax are open and whether anyone is entitled to a share. Courtesy notices from the Revenue Commissioner may never have reached you, so do not assume a quiet mailbox means a clear account.

Next, secure the property. Change the locks if keys are unaccounted for, check the roof and the water shut-off, and photograph each room. That record protects you if a question comes up later. Keep the utilities on if you can, since buyers walk through with lights on.

Finally, put all the heirs on one conversation. Disagreements about price and timing are common, and a sale needs every signature. Share the tax figures with everyone so the numbers are not a surprise at closing.

The title company or attorney takes the lead once you accept an offer. It searches the title, obtains payoffs from the Revenue Commissioner and any lender, and prepares a settlement statement. You review it, sign the deed and receive the balance after taxes, payoffs and recording costs come off.

Plan to bring photo identification and keys. If the property is in a city that straddles the county line, tell the closing agent which side of the line it is on, so the deed goes to the right probate office. After closing, the buyer assesses the property with the Revenue Commissioner, so that part is no longer your task. You should still keep your closing papers and the final tax receipt for your records.

Retail sales ask a lot of a seller. You clean, repair, stage, host showings and then wait for a buyer's lender to finish an appraisal. Any of those steps can fall through. A cash sale removes the lender, so the date is set by the title work and your own schedule.

That suits sellers who are moving fast, carrying a second house or looking at a May tax sale. It also suits an owner whose house has deferred repairs, since we take it as is. We will explain exactly how an offer is figured and what comes out at closing, so you can compare it with listing the house and decide for yourself.

faqs.q: Who bills and collects property tax in Elmore County?
faqs.a: The Elmore County Revenue Commissioner, whose office combines assessing and collecting. It is at 100 E. Commerce Street, Suite 102, Wetumpka, phone 334-567-1184.

faqs.q: When are Elmore County property taxes due?
faqs.a: October 1. They become delinquent after December 31.

faqs.q: What is the county seat of Elmore County?
faqs.a: Wetumpka. Millbrook is the largest city.

faqs.q: What is the deed tax on an Elmore County sale?
faqs.a: Fifty cents for each $500 of value under Alabama Code 40-22-1, plus the probate recording fee.

faqs.q: Is Elmore County part of the Montgomery area?
faqs.a: Yes. It lies just north of Montgomery and belongs to the Montgomery metropolitan area.
